summary: Describes uses and conventions for IETF working groups considering GitHub, such as setting up and administering repositories and teams. It does not mandate any process and does not require changes for groups that do not use GitHub. It is informational.

eli5.summary: If a team uses a shared website for its work, someone must set it up and manage who can do what. This document explains how that setup and management usually goes.

questions: how to administer a working group github organization
how to back up working group github repositories
subtitle: Conventions for IETF working groups using GitHub to manage their work.

tldr.problem: IETF working groups increasingly use GitHub to develop standards, but there was no uniform way to set up and manage GitHub organizations for this purpose.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 8875 specifies administrative processes and conventions for creating GitHub organizations, managing personnel, archiving content, and handling document repositories in a consistent way across working groups.
tldr.outcome: Working groups can now use GitHub in a reviewed, validated way with proper backup and archiving of all official interactions.

today: RFC 8875 is an Internet Standard Track informational document. It describes processes that working groups can adopt voluntarily; it does not mandate any changes to the IETF standards process or require all working groups to use GitHub.

sections.title: Why Working Groups Use GitHub
sections.content: Many IETF working groups use GitHub to manage their document development. Some groups are unfamiliar with how to get started or unsure which conventions to follow. This RFC specifies a uniform way to create and manage GitHub organizations for working groups that want to use it, without requiring changes to groups that do not use GitHub or use other services like GitLab or Bitbucket.
sections.eli5: Some work teams want to use GitHub to share their documents. This guide tells them how to set it up the right way.

sections.title: Setting Up and Running a Working Group Organization
sections.content:
When a working group chair or area director requests a GitHub organization, a sequence of steps is initiated. First, an organization is created with a name starting with ietf-wg- followed by the working group name. The IETF Secretariat and area directors are designated as owners. A team with administrator access is created for the working group chairs and secretary.

The RFC also specifies how to handle migrations of existing organizations, personnel changes, working group closures, and creation of document repositories. Document authors are identified as collaborators, and repositories are configured with skeleton files and continuous integration support.
sections.eli5: The organization name follows a pattern, and specific people get different levels of access to manage it. When people change roles or the group closes, these permissions are updated.

sections.title: Working Group Practices and Content Management
sections.content:
Every repository must include boilerplate text from the IETF license for open-source repositories, incorporated into the CONTRIBUTING file. Working groups can store multiple drafts in a single repository if they are closely linked.

A key requirement is that all official IETF working group interactions must be archived. The RFC specifies using the Git protocol to back up every GitHub repository to an IETF-maintained mirror server. A service will fetch repositories every hour, and the system will also back up GitHub issues and pull requests using the GitHub API.
sections.eli5: The team keeps standard instructions in the repository about how people can contribute. Everything that happens is backed up to another server so nothing is lost.

sections.title: Security and Data Protection
sections.content:
The RFC identifies two main security concerns. First, an attacker who can change Internet-Drafts late in a working group's process could cause unnoticed changes in protocols that are eventually adopted. Second, there is a risk of data loss due to centralization of data in one service.

Both risks are mitigated by the plan described in Section 3.2: automatic hourly backups of all repositories to an IETF-maintained server, ensuring that content is preserved and recoverable even if GitHub experiences an outage or deletion.
sections.eli5: Someone could try to sneak a bad change into a draft right before it becomes a standard. That is prevented by keeping backups of everything.

sections.title: Manual and Automated Implementation
sections.content:
The RFC deliberately leaves unspecified whether these administrative processes should be performed manually by the IETF Secretariat or automated by scripts. Two working examples are cited: the ietf-gh-scripts and i-d-template projects, both of which are in use in existing working groups.

The RFC also notes that most of the conventions are drawn from RFC 8874, which provides broader guidance on how working groups use GitHub.
sections.eli5: The processes can be done by hand or by automatic scripts; the RFC does not pick one way. Some groups have already shared their automation examples for others to use.

references.text: Thomson, M. and B. Stark, "Working Group GitHub Usage Guidance", RFC 8874, DOI 10.17487/RFC8874, August 2020.
